ab_punk_wall.blurb: Punk Wall is the best-known wall in Black Feather Canyon, a side canyon inside Banff National Park above Lake Minnewanka. It is a bolted limestone face with about twenty single-pitch sport routes, mostly in the 5.10 range with a solid handful of 5.11 to 5.12 and a few lines into the low 5.13s; there is very little for beginners. The stone is water-worn and sloper-rich, with edges and some mineral staining, and a few loose flakes are possible. The wall faces south and catches strong sun, so early or late in the day suits warmer weather. The approach crosses wildlife corridors and bear sightings are common, so carry bear spray and make noise.

ab_roadside_attraction.blurb: Roadside Attraction is a small single-pitch sport crag on the north side of Canyon Creek in the Moose Mountain area of Kananaskis, west of Bragg Creek. Routes are short, roughly 40 to 60 feet, on generally sound limestone with well-kept bolts. Nearly everything sits between 5.10 and 5.11, so it suits climbers comfortable on moderate-to-hard sport lines rather than beginners. The cliff leans south but picks up shade through parts of the day. Spring through early fall is the comfortable window; after rain or snowmelt, gravel and damp rock can be a nuisance. A footpath beside a quiet access road leads in, and weekends can bring company.

ab_black_flag.blurb: Black Flag is one of the newer Moose Mountain sectors in Kananaskis, sitting north of the road in between the longer-established Dust Bowl and Moose Patch. The wall faces south and warms up early, which fits the mountain's reputation for extending the season into spring and fall. Routes here are bolted sport lines, with a steep central section holding long, demanding climbs and easier but still hard lines on either side. This area has mostly 5.11 to 5.13, with one harder. The rock is better than average for the mountain. From the Moose Patch trail, walk west along the cliff base for about five minutes.
